The shimazu-clan dossier (jk-01-x) runs 1576-1600 and closes into this one.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: a domain inside the Tokugawa realm, which Cliopatria draws only as part of Warring States Japan and the Tokugawa Shogunate. The infobox gives the provinces and 770,000 koku (second only to Kaga), no area. Kagoshima Prefecture (mainland cells, about 8,600 km2 by the gazetteer) plus a 30 km circle at Miyakonojō for the Hyūga share (the page does not name the district; confidence 2). The infobox map shows the 1586 maximum, not this extent.

keyframe_review.note: The same land plus Amami Ōshima and the northern islands 'annexed into Satsuma Domain' (Invasion of Ryukyu page, no year; the oaths and terms were signed in 1611). ledger.note: 1600: the Satsuma Domain. Infobox 'Established: 1600'; the Shimazu 'fought on the losing side' at Sekigahara in 1600 and Shimazu Iehisa is first daimyō from 1602. Provinces 'Satsuma, Ōsumi, Hyūga'; the Hyūga share is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Okinawa Island and the Ryukyu Kingdom

ledger.note: 1609: Satsuma lands in Ryukyu. The fleet of about 100 ships left on 4 March, reached Amami Ōshima on 7 April and Unten harbour on Okinawa on 25 April; Shimazu Iehisa had 'requested permission from the shogunate to invade Ryukyu'.
1609: Shuri falls. Satsuma officers 'entered the castle' on 5 May and began an inventory of its treasures; Shō Nei left Unten for Satsuma on 17 May; infobox 'Satsuma victory'.

region.text: the Ryukyu Kingdom, conquered 'as a vassal state'

ledger.note: 1609: the Ryukyu Kingdom becomes a vassal. The Satsuma page: the domain 'conquered the Ryukyu Kingdom as a vassal state' after the 1609 invasion; Invasion page infobox 'Ryukyu becomes a vassal state'; the 1611 oaths call the islands 'a feudal dependency of Satsuma'. Ryukyu remained 'nominally independent'.

region.text: Amami Ōshima and the northern islands

ledger.note: 1611: Amami Ōshima and the northern islands annexed. 'Amami Ōshima and other northern islands, now the Satsunan Islands, were annexed into Satsuma Domain'; the Satsuma page: the peace treaty let Satsuma annex 'the Amami and Tokara Islands'. Neither page gives the year; 1611 is the year of the surrender documents signed at Kagoshima (confidence 1).

1871: Satsuma's overlordship ends with the domain. The page: the han system was abolished in 1871 and 'the following year' the government told King Shō Tai he was Domain Head of Ryukyu Domain, moving authority to Tokyo. The ryukyu-kingdom dossier ends its Satsuma vassalage in October 1872; this one ends with the domain.

wars.name: Invasion of Ryukyu

zones.text: Okinawa Island and the Ryukyu Kingdom

wars.outcome: Satsuma victory: Shuri taken in May 1609, Shō Nei carried to Kagoshima and made to swear oaths in 1610-1611; Ryukyu became a vassal and Satsuma annexed the Amami Islands.

wars.name: Battle of Sekigahara
wars.outcome: The Shimazu fought on the losing side but kept their land; no territory changed hands for Satsuma.
wars.note: Page: the Shimazu fought on the losing side at the decisive battle of Sekigahara in 1600; Shimazu Iehisa is the first daimyō from 1602. The campaign is the tokugawa-shogunate dossier's start.

wars.name: Boshin War
wars.outcome: Satsuma fought on the imperial side (Toba-Fushimi, 1868); the last shogunate forces were defeated in 1869. No Satsuma land changed.

certainty.note: Provincial and domain boundaries are not surveyed on the page; the Ryukyu relation is a vassalage, not a border.

notes: Written by jk-01-x on 2026-10-19 from two pages (Satsuma Domain, Invasion of Ryukyu). Satsuma is a han inside the Tokugawa realm: the tokugawa-shogunate dossier (jk-01-c) records the 1609 contest and the 1609 vassalage of Ryukyu against 'ryukyu-kingdom' as if the shogunate did it, and the ryukyu-kingdom dossier (jk-01-b) records the same events against 'satsuma-domain'; this dossier mirrors the ryukyu-kingdom side (counterpart 'ryukyu-kingdom' in vassal_start 1609/5, as the schema says the vassal is the counterpart), so the renderer should take the Ryukyu overlordship from here and from ryukyu-kingdom, and drop the duplicate in tokugawa-shogunate. Vassal_end: this dossier 1871 (the han is abolished); ryukyu-kingdom has October 1872 (Ryukyu Domain): a one-year difference to settle. Territory: no area on the page; the Hyūga share (Morokata/Miyakonojō) is not named on the page ('Province: Satsuma, Ōsumi, Hyūga'); the infobox 'Maximum extent ... 1586' is the Sengoku Shimazu, not the han (a shimazu-clan dossier for 1570s-1600 would cover it). The Tokara Islands are annexed with Amami but too small for the grid. Gazetteer: no 'Miyakonojo' place, a coordinate circle is used. Not on the page: 1611 for Amami, Morokata, Tsurumaru, the 1866 Satsuma-Chōshū alliance; the 1862 Namamugi Incident and the 1863 bombardment of Kagoshima are on the page without the other party, so no war entry is made for them.
